newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique signs oil exploration deal with BP.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique signs oil exploration deal with BP.

text.p: The Mozambican government has signed an agreement with British Petroleum (BP) for oil exploration covering an offshore area of about 80,000 square km in the delta of the Zambezi river, Radio Mozambique said on Tuesday.

It said the agreement was signed on Monday by Minister of Mineral Resources and Energy John Kachamila, the general manager of the National Hydrocarbons Company (ENH) Issufo Abdullah, and BP general manager for West Africa, David Bamford.

The agreement covers six months of initial surveys. During this time BP will mainly be looking at existing geological, geophysical and geochemical data to see if they can verify the existence of oil-bearing seeps on the sea bed.

Previous prospecting in the Zambezi delta, undertaken by the Norwegian company GECO in the 1980s, produced no firm results. But GECO was concerned with shallow water zones, while BP is interested in areas where the water is up to 2,000 metres deep.
During the initial six-month period, a production sharing agreement will be negotiated between ENH and BP, which will cover half the initial exploration area.
If the initial results are positive, further and more extensive surveys relying largely on seismic methods will be carried out over the next two years.
"If results continue to be positive, we would then shoot 3D seismic data, and maybe sink some wells," Bamford was quoted as saying.
